survived.title: slugify_room_name has no uniqueness guarantee and nothing enforces one — two rooms can share a slug, and on Roborock the second one dispatches to the FIRST one's segment id
survived.mechanism: slugify_room_name (rooms/utils.py:35) deletes ' and ", maps & -> "and", and space -> "_". I executed it on real inputs: 'Bedroom'/'Bedroom' -> 'bedroom'; 'Bed & Bath'/'Bed and Bath' -> 'bed_and_bath'; 'Kids Room'/'Kids_Room' -> 'kids_room'; "Cat's Room"/'Cats Room' -> 'cats_room'; '"Guest" Room'/'Guest Room' -> 'guest_room'. The docstring at rooms/utils.py:16-18 CLAIMS the invariant 'distinct names must yield distinct slugs' — the code does not have it, and no caller enforces it. discover_rooms_for_vacuum dedupes ONLY by numeric room_id (seen_room_ids, room_discovery.py:223/240) and then stamps 'slug': slugify_room_name(name) at :254 with no collision check, so both rooms are emitted with the same slug. Two consequences, both silent: (1) WRONG PHYSICAL ROOM on Roborock — dispatch/manager.py:285-291 builds slug_to_live_id first-wins ('if not slug or slug in slug_to_live_id: continue'), so the colliding room's live id is never registered; at :306 the second room's target slug resolves to the FIRST room's live segment id, is appended to new_segments, and dispatched. The 'dropped' warning path at :310 is NOT reached because the lookup succeeds, so there is no log line at all. Selecting both rooms yields new_segments=[16,16]. (2) STORED DATA DESTROYED on both brands — plan_migration (reconciliation.py:178-179, 210) builds existing_by_slug with setdefault (first-wins); on a confirmed migrate both discovered rooms resolve to the SAME source dict and both get carried with identical durable settings (profile, floor_type, grants_access_to, rules, color), while the second stored room's config is overwritten and is NOT reported in 'dropped' (dropped is derived from existing_by_slug at :247-251, which never contained it). Room attribution during a run is also first-wins by slug (jobs/active_job.py:1158-1164).
survived.user_impact: A user with two rooms whose names collide under slugify (two 'Bedroom's, or 'Bed & Bath' vs 'Bed and Bath') selects room B and the robot cleans room A instead, with no warning in the log and no error in the UI. On a confirmed re-map, room B's per-room settings, access grants and rules are permanently replaced by room A's and never listed as dropped.

survived.title: discover_rooms_for_vacuum's single-map fallback serves ANOTHER map's room list and relabels it with the REQUESTED map_id, defeating the map_id filter at both room writers
survived.mechanism: For service_response brands (Roborock), room_discovery.py:174-180 does 'segments = per_map.get(str(resolved_map_id))' and, when that misses, 'if segments is None and len(per_map) == 1: segments = next(iter(per_map.values()))' — it takes whatever single map is cached WITHOUT checking that it is the map that was asked for. Every room built from those segments is then stamped '"map_id": str(resolved_map_id)' at :251 — the REQUESTED id, not the source cache key. That relabelling defeats the only guard the write path has: room_crud.save_managed_rooms:239-241 and rebuild_map:418-420 filter 'str(room.get("map_id")) == str(map_id)', which can never fail because the label was applied from the request. save_managed_rooms:261 then does 'map_bucket["rooms"] = managed_rooms' — a wholesale replacement of the real map's stored rooms with the other map's rooms. Reaching len(per_map)==1 with two real maps is concrete: source_refresh.flatten_maps_response:205 writes 'out[map_name] = seg_list', so two maps that resolve to the SAME key (both unnamed with the same 'flag', or both renamed to the same name in the app) collapse to one entry with no warning; and async_refresh_room_source:249-254/264-272 swallows every failure and leaves the PREVIOUS cache in place, so a cache captured when the user had one map survives after a second map is added. The same mislabelled list also feeds dispatch/manager.py:282-291, where slug_to_live_id is then built from the wrong floor's segments.
survived.user_impact: On a multi-map (multi-floor) Roborock, importing or re-saving one floor writes the OTHER floor's rooms into that floor's bucket, destroying its stored per-room settings; and a live-id dispatch resolves 'bedroom' to the other floor's segment id, so the robot cleans the wrong floor's room. No error is surfaced — the map_id on every room looks correct because it was stamped from the request.

survived.title: A room name that slugifies to empty passes discovery's only validation and is then silently deleted by plan_migration and silently un-cleanable by dispatch
survived.mechanism: discover_rooms_for_vacuum validates the NAME ('name = str(raw_name).strip(); if not name: continue' at :245-248) but never validates the SLUG it derives at :254. Because slugify_room_name deletes ' and ", a name composed only of quote characters survives the name check and yields ''. I executed slugify on "'", '\"', "'''" and ' \" ' — all return ''. Downstream, empty slug is treated as 'no identity': plan_migration (reconciliation.py:207-208) does 'if new_id is None or not slug: continue', so the room is excluded from new_rooms and its durable settings are dropped — and it is not reported in 'dropped' either, because _room_slug returned '' so it never entered existing_by_slug (reconciliation.py:178-179, dropped built at :247-251). compute_reconciliation skips it identically at :106. dispatch/manager.py:305-310 reads the target slug '' and looks it up in slug_to_live_id, which never contains '' (skipped at :288), so the room is dropped from the run. Same class of gap: the slug docstring asserts non-empty slugs as an invariant of the transform, but the transform's own character deletions can produce one and the single validation point does not check it.
survived.user_impact: A room named with only punctuation loses every stored setting permanently and without any 'dropped' report the moment the user confirms a re-map, and on Roborock it can never be cleaned — it is silently skipped from every run.

survived.title: Drift keys its history by bare device room_id across ALL maps but feeds it only the ACTIVE map's discovery, so a multi-map vacuum's inactive rooms decay toward 'removed' and colliding ids mask each other
survived.mechanism: run_discovery_pass calls discover_rooms_for_vacuum(hass, vacuum_entity_id=...) with NO map_id (drift.py:540), so room_discovery.py:168 resolves to the ACTIVE map only and returns that map's rooms. The resulting discovered_ids set is handed to update_drift_history (drift.py:278-337), whose history dict is keyed by 'str(rid)' — a bare device room_id with no map qualifier — and whose configured set (_list_configured_room_ids, drift.py:233-247) unions is_configured room ids across EVERY map for the vacuum. The device room_id namespace is per-map (both brands number segments from ~1/16 per map), so on a two-map vacuum: (a) every configured room of the inactive map that has no id-twin on the active map gets missing_passes incremented on every pass (drift.py:322-329) and eventually reports as removed; (b) rooms on different maps that share a numeric id are the SAME history entry, so an inactive-map room is marked 'seen' by its active-map namesake and its genuine removal is never detected; (c) _room_lookup (drift.py:250-275) does 'out[rid] = {...}' across all maps, so the name/map_id shown for a drifted id is whichever map iterated last. Nothing in the pass is map-scoped.
survived.user_impact: A user with an upstairs and a downstairs map is repeatedly told that the rooms on whichever floor is not currently active have been removed from the vacuum, with the wrong floor's name attached; and a room genuinely deleted on one floor is never reported because a same-numbered room on the other floor keeps resetting its counter.

survived.title: Reconciliation never runs in production: no trigger, no schedule, no UI — the reviews are computed into a payload nothing reads
survived.mechanism: compute_reconciliation has exactly ONE caller: RoomMapManager.discover_rooms (room_crud.py:68), which is reachable only through the eufy_vacuum.discover_rooms service (core/manager.py:1426 -> services/rooms.py:140). Nothing in the shipped card calls that service: grep of src/ for 'discover_rooms' returns only the unused constant declaration src/constants.js:59, and grep of the BUILT bundles (custom_components/eufy_vacuum/frontend/eufy-vacuum-command-center.js and eufy-vacuum-cards.js) for 'reconcile_room' returns 0 hits and for 'reconciliation' returns 0 hits — the payload["reconciliation"] block is never rendered and the reconcile_room service is never invoked by any shipped UI. The AUTOMATIC discovery path does not compute reconciliation either: listeners/discovery.py:86-87 calls async_refresh_room_source + setup/drift.run_discovery_pass, and run_discovery_pass (drift.py:538-550) calls discover_rooms_for_vacuum directly and only bumps drift counters. So on the vacuum_docked / active_map_changed / 6-hour-periodic triggers, an id renumber or a rename is never compared against stored rooms at all. There is no schedule, no repair-flow, and no sensor attribute exposing the reviews. Net: after a Roborock re-segment, stored ids diverge from live ids permanently and silently; the ONLY thing that would tell the user is a service call they have no way to know to make, and the only thing that would fix attribution (plan_migration) is unreachable from the product.
survived.user_impact: Stored room ids stay permanently diverged from the device's live ids after any re-segment. Every id-keyed consumer (floor-type confirmations, access-graph grants, rule status, per-room settings, room history) stays bound to the wrong physical room, and the user is never told anything changed — this is the upstream cause of the campaign's DQ-DE-1 wrong-room dispatch.

survived.title: Two rooms with the same name collapse into one identity: phantom id_changed on an unchanged map, and migrate overwrites one room's settings with the other's
survived.mechanism: Slug is the load-bearing identity key but nothing enforces slug uniqueness anywhere: slugify_room_name (rooms/utils.py:35) does no disambiguation, discovery dedupes by room_id ONLY (room_discovery.py:240-243), and build_managed_rooms keys by id and never inspects slugs. survived.title: No in-flight coalescing or lock on the refresh: triggers spawn unbounded concurrent get_maps cloud calls, and an older response landing last becomes the resident cached snapshot — including one that started before a map switch and lands after it

Each task independently awaits `roborock.get_maps` — a cloud call — so N triggers make N cloud calls, and a rate-limited/timed-out call is precisely the input that produces SRC-1's silent stale serve. Separately, because line 280's write is unconditional last-writer-wins, a refresh that STARTED earlier and finishes later overwrites a newer snapshot; that older snapshot then stays resident until the next trigger. The map-switch variant is worse than a plain revert: `_active_map_id_from_config` is evaluated at line 278, i.e. AFTER the await returns, so a refresh whose get_maps response was captured BEFORE a map switch is keyed using the POST-switch active map name in the len(maps)==1 branch (line 183) — the old map's rooms are cached under the new map's name.

survived.title: Mid-run reachability is queue-scoped while preflight is graph-scoped — a run that omits the dock room reports EVERY remaining room as access_blocked and can cancel the job
survived.mechanism:
rooms/access_graph.py exports the EDGES (_build_room_access_views, :236-276) but never the reachability ANSWER, so each consumer re-implements traversal and they disagree.

Preflight (run_plan.py:1132-1148) computes accessibility over ALL managed rooms: seeds = {rid in all_rooms_by_id if not requires_map.get(rid)} then a fixpoint over requires_map with no membership filter. A room reachable only through an UNSELECTED transit room is therefore correctly accessible.

The mid-run sibling (run_plan.py:1615-1637) restricts the same computation to the queue: the seed comprehension iterates queue_room_ids only, and the propagation step filters parent_ids to `parent_id in queue_room_id_set` (:1628-1632). Critically the seed TEST still uses the GLOBAL requires_map (:1618), so a queued room whose parent is outside the queue is neither a seed nor reachable by propagation — it can never become accessible.

In a graph the validator calls valid, every non-dock room has exactly one inbound edge (access_graph.py:767-778 raises missing_dependency otherwise), so the ONLY room that can seed at :1615 is the dock room. Consequence: if the dock room is not enabled for this run, accessible_room_ids is empty and every remaining room falls into affected_remaining_rooms with reason 'access_blocked' and blocked_by_room_id=None (:1650-1672).

Worse, this fires with no blocker rule matching. The direct_blocked scan at :1570-1582 also walks queue_room_ids only, so blocker_rules_present stays False when the only blocker rule lives on an unqueued transit room — which disarms the bail-out at :1608-1613. listeners/path_blockers.py:196 subscribes to that rule's entity regardless, so any state change on it (:116 only rejects old_state == new_state) invokes the report.

Walked concretely: valid tree Dock(1)->Hall(2)->Bed(3), Dock flagged is_dock_room, a blocker rule on Hall watching binary_sensor.door. User enables only Bed. Preflight: seeds {1}, propagates to {1,2,3}, Bed included, job starts with queue_room_ids=[3]. Door sensor changes state (to ANY value). Runtime report: no structural issues, queue=[3], remaining=[3], direct_blocked={} (Hall not walked), blocker_rules_present=False, seeds={} because requires_map[3]==[2], propagation filters parent 2 out of the queue set -> accessible={} -> Bed reported access_blocked. listeners/path_blockers.py:143-157 then applies path_block_action verbatim: pause_and_event pauses the job, cancel_and_event cancels it and fires EVENT_JOB_FINISHED + EVENT_RUN_INCOMPLETE.
survived.user_impact: A perfectly valid access graph plus a normal partial run (user cleans the bedroom, not the entryway the dock sits in) turns any watched blocker entity's state change into a spurious 'path blocked' verdict on every unfinished room. With path_block_action=cancel_and_event the run is aborted mid-clean and the rooms are never cleaned; with pause_and_event the robot stops until the pause timeout. The event names no blocking room (blocked_by_room_id=None), so the user cannot diagnose it. On event_only it still fires a false EVENT_PATH_BLOCKED that user automations act on.

And I read listeners/path_blockers.register: watch_map is built from every room on every map regardless of enabled/queue state, so the rule entity IS subscribed. blocked_by_room_id is None because parent_ids is empty after the queue filter. pause/cancel act on the report with no re-verification.

killed.title: _access_graph_state fails OPEN to 'blank', so a numeric-slot rebuild that wipes the access graph, dock flag and blocker rules leaves the next run silently unconstrained
killed.mechanism:
_access_graph_state's first branch is `if not has_dock and not has_grants: return 'blank'` (:864-873), and 'blank' is the ALLOW state — run_plan.py:983-994 only blocks blank when rules also exist (`graph_state == 'blank' and any_rules`). The state is therefore indistinguishable between 'user never configured a graph' and 'the graph was just erased', and the fallback is permissive.

Erasure is reachable through the shipped rebuild_map service. rebuild_map_bucket (maps/map_manager.py:144-199) matches previous settings by NUMERIC SLOT only: `previous = existing_rooms.get(room_id_key, {})` (:148), then :192-195 take is_dock_room, grants_access_to and rules from that `previous`. When a re-segment renumbers ids — the shipped Roborock identity behaviour, where segment ids renumber and identity is the name slug — every discovered id misses its previous entry, so every room is rebuilt with is_dock_room=False, grants_access_to=[] and rules=[] at once. has_dock and has_grants both go False, _access_graph_state returns 'blank', any_rules is also False (the rules went with them), and the next run proceeds with no access constraints and no blocker rules, with no warning anywhere.

The integration already has the correct implementation for this exact situation and does not use it here: rooms/reconciliation.py::plan_migration matches by slug with an id-collision guard (:186-215) and explicitly rewrites grants_access_to through the old->new id remap, dropping only targets that no longer resolve (:230-245). rooms/room_crud.py exposes both — reconcile_room (:81-215) uses plan_migration, rebuild_map (:403-428) uses the numeric-slot rebuild_map_bucket — so which of the two the user happens to invoke decides whether their access graph and blocker rules survive.
killed.user_impact: A Roborock user who re-segments and then uses Rebuild map (rather than the reconcile/re-map flow) loses the dock room, every access link and every blocker rule in one silent step, and the very next run cleans everything selected with none of those gates applied — including a room the user had gated behind a blocker rule such as 'do not enter while the baby is asleep'. Nothing reports the loss: the graph simply reads as never-configured. Eufy is exposed on the narrower case where a re-map merges or drops rooms and frees their ids.
